# Further Reading {#sec-further-reading}

Each entry was read for this book at the depth logged in the repository's `research-log.md`;
the note says what it is good for. Recent and contested results are in the chapters, with
their dates.

## Data collection, labels and cleaning

- @gebru2018datasheets: the questions a dataset's documentation should answer, from
  motivation to maintenance.
- @cetinkayarundel2024ims: an introductory statistics text with clear chapters on sampling
  designs and observational data.
- @northcutt2019confident: confident learning, with its assumptions stated.
- @vanbuuren2018fimd: missing-data mechanisms and multiple imputation, in depth and free
  online.
- @kuhn2019feature: a practical book on encodings, transformations and feature selection
  (read for its scope, not in full).

## The training distribution

- @saerens2002adjusting: adjusting a classifier's probabilities to new class priors, and
  estimating those priors by EM.
- @chawla2002smote: SMOTE, defined.
- @morenotorres2012unifying: definitions of covariate, prior-probability and concept shift.

## How much data, and which

- @viering2021shape: a survey of learning-curve shapes, including the cases that are not power
  laws.
- @hutter2021learning: the exact model behind [Why Power Laws](chapters/13-why-power-laws.qmd#sec-long-tail).
- @dohmatob2024tale: Hutter's model trained on a distribution with its tail cut, the theory of
  model collapse on a long tail.
- @michaud2023quantization: the quantization model, linking power-law frequencies of skills to
  power-law scaling.
- @hoffmann2022training and @muennighoff2023scaling: compute-optimal allocation, and what
  repeated data is worth.
- @sorscher2022beyond: when to keep hard examples and when easy ones, derived and measured.
- @settles2009active: a survey of active learning, from uncertainty sampling onward.
